case: Hinterkaifeck murders (official address: Groebern Nr. 27 1/2, Gemeinde Wangen, Lkr. Schrobenhausen, Oberbayern)
method_notes: Primary file StAM Pol.Dir. Muenchen 8091b not accessed directly; relied on the 2026 Bavarian State Archives exhibition catalog which quotes it with page references.
Contemporary newspapers used via transcriptions in the Hinterkaifeck-Wiki; original digitized pages not checked (limitation).
SNIPPET-ONLY marks claims seen only in search-result text. [unverified] marks claims not anchorable to a fetched source.
Source register ids [n] correspond to ledger.json and the Sources block of HINTERKAIFECK_REPORT.md.

victims.name: Viktoria Gabriel geb. Gruber
victims.role: widowed daughter, farmholder (Guetergemeinschaft with Karl Gabriel)

victims.name: Josef Gruber
victims.role: illegitimate grandson; paternity disputed (Schlittenbauer vs Andreas Gruber)

victims.name: Maria Baumgartner
victims.role: maid, arrived on the murder day ~16:30

established_facts.claim: Six persons killed by massive head injuries, night 31 Mar - 1 Apr 1922; found 4 Apr 1922

Weapon: Reuthaue belonging to the farm, made by Andreas Gruber, found Feb 1923 in a Fehlboden; identified via protruding screw matching round wound on Viktoria's head; destroyed in the 1944 Augsburg bombing
Bodies: 4 in the barn (Stadel) covered with hay and a wooden door; maid covered with feather bed; red skirt over child's broken carriage
Autopsies 6-8 Apr 1922 by Gerichtsarzt Aumüller; Caezilia Gruber 7 blows plus strangulation marks; skulls detached and lost since
Hard currency left (1880 GM gold + 1700 RM silver found by court commission); paper money missing, amount unknown
Scene contaminated by onlookers before police arrival; tracker dog took no scent
Over 100 investigative proceedings by 6.11.1926 (Pielmayer) and >100 by 1930; no indictment ever; official closure reported 1955
Weapon initially suspected (Kreuzhacke/Spitzhacke in feed barrier) ruled out on wound patterns at the 7.4.1922 Leichenbeschau

attributed_claims.claim: Death window: clothing state implies 20-22h on 31 Mar; GDA says 19-22h; MZ 7.4.1922 says 20-21h; Reingruber 20-23h; minority Saturday-evening view (Meiendres 1948)
Killer(s) remained on/returned to farm 1-4 Apr: bread consumed, broth on stove, meat freshly cut, cattle fed/watered/milked, chimney smoke 1 Apr
attributed_claims.reliability: strong (multiple independent observations of effects); duration inferred

attributed_claims.claim: Pre-murder anomalies: footprints toward farm 30 Mar with none leading away; attic noises; missing house key; unsubscribed Munich newspaper; feeling of being watched from the woods
attributed_claims.reliability: single report chain (Gruber to hearers, StAM 8091b S.1034); embellishments grew within a week (MZ 7.4.1922)

attributed_claims.claim: Attic straw bedding with body-shaped moulds; two displaced roof tiles with overwatch view; rope from loft - pre-murder or post-murder hiding place
attributed_claims.reliability: Wiesner protocol inference; timing of use unknown

attributed_claims.claim: Scream test by Wiesner commission: shouts in the barn inaudible in the maid's room
Schlittenbauer's 1925 'frozen ground' remark to teacher Yblagger at the ruins; 'Ich-Form' Stammtisch anecdote; key/door contradiction between his 1922 and 1931 statements
attributed_claims.reliability: later-recorded anecdotes + file-internal contradiction; innocent readings documented

attributed_claims.claim: 2000 Wiest operational case analysis: gain excluded, personal/emotional conflict central, coverings suggest perpetrator-victim relationship; Viktoria deposited 700 M in a confessional 17.3.1922
attributed_claims.reliability: single modern analysis of a partial, twice-reconstructed file

attributed_claims.claim: June 2007 Fürstenfeldbruck police-academy student project: one prime suspect identified, name withheld; project leader later publicly doubted her group's conclusion
attributed_claims.reliability: known only via BR-broadcast quote; report not accessible

attributed_claims.claim: Previous maid quit autumn 1921 because the farm was 'haunted'
attributed_claims.reliability: SNIPPET-ONLY, 1997 press; no pre-1997 file statement found; her documented 1922 statement concerns a 1920 burglary [7]

attributed_claims.claim: Mid-May 1927: midnight stranger confesses to a Waidhofen resident and flees
attributed_claims.reliability: single anecdote, likely Leuschner-line; no file document located

inferences.claim: Victims lured into the barn one by one, possibly via a deliberately loosened cow
Perpetrator(s) familiar with the farm: hid the weapon where only demolition found it; navigated silently; concealed exits
inferences.status: consistent with insider OR long-hiding outsider

inferences.claim: Robbery motive progressively abandoned by investigators; Wiest 2000 excludes gain
inferences.status: expert assessment, not provable (paper money value unknown)

speculation.claim: Multiple perpetrators (explicitly left open in the archival catalog)
'Man from the Train' serial-killer mapping (Bill James 2017)
speculation.note: framework hypothesis, no file anchorage found [unverified]

speculation.claim: Post-WWII POW-officer story as cover for Karl Gabriel's survival
speculation.note: the one sourced eyewitness story (Eser 1951) was retracted as a lie under official investigation

suspects.name: Lorenz Schlittenbauer
suspects.basis: affair with Viktoria; blocked marriage; sworn paternity reversals 1919; closest residence; anomalous discovery behaviour; 1925 frozen-ground remark; slander suits vs Sigl and others
suspects.supporting: documented motive history + opportunity + behavioural anomalies [2][3][6][7][9]
suspects.challenging: police 1930 assessment: no financial or reputational damage from the guardianship dispute; well-regarded; scene behaviour explicable by concern for the child [2]; zero physical or witness linkage
suspects.falsifier: alibi for 31 Mar evening / proven third-party theft of identifiable item / document showing paternity matter definitively closed in his favour

suspects.name: Karl Gabriel (returned-dead theory)
suspects.challenging: comrade Brummer: '...ihn hat eine Mine getötet.' (StAM 8091b S.568) [2]; Eser story retracted as lie [2][6]
suspects.falsifier: already near-falsified; only a documented post-1914 identity swap would revive it

suspects.name: Josef Bärtl ('Eiserner Heindl')
suspects.basis: escaped 1921 from Günzburg psychiatric hospital; 1926 warrant 'dringender Tatverdacht'; identified by a clairvoyant
suspects.challenging: never caught, whereabouts on the night never established; spiritualist identification worthless

suspects.name: Adolf and Anton Gump (+Dreßel, Musweiler, Friedrich/Fischer)
suspects.basis: wanted from 9.4.1922 for Oberschlesien farm murders (Freikorps context); 1951 deathbed accusation by sister Kreszentia Mayer
suspects.supporting: Reingruber wanted notice incl. alibi check for 30 Mar-1 Apr 1922 [6][7]
suspects.challenging: Anton briefly in custody 1951, released; proceedings dropped 1954 for lack of proof [6][7]; Adolf died 1944

suspects.name: Others in the file (Bichler brothers, Thaler brothers, Georg Siegl, Schreyer brothers, Peter Weber, Kaltenecker/Schweiger/Schnepf, Hofner, Pfleger, Lackermeier, etc.)
suspects.basis: theft records, denunciations, one-day alibi gaps, anonymous letters
suspects.supporting: individually weak; Weber's 1919/20 remark about 'gold to get at Kaifeck' (Betz 7.4.1922) is the most concrete pre-crime statement [7]
suspects.challenging: most closed for proven innocence or absence of any record; one denouncer (Seidl) convicted of false accusation [7]
suspects.status: collectively: the outsider class the police first pursued

hypotheses_ranked.name: Personal-conflict killing by perpetrator(s) closely familiar with farm and family
hypotheses_ranked.criteria: documentary anchorage; independent corroboration; behavioural fit; falsifiability; disconfirming evidence
hypotheses_ranked.support: Wiest 2000 gain-exclusion and conflict assessment [2]; coverings; silent navigation; weapon concealment; Viktoria's 700 M confessional deposit as tension signal [2]
hypotheses_ranked.challenge: each behavioural indicator has an innocent reading; unknown value of missing paper money; multiple perpetrators open
hypotheses_ranked.would_falsify: precise probate accounting showing only insignificant paper money missing + outsider theft of a traceable item
hypotheses_ranked.uncertainty: high; explanation-family, not a named person

hypotheses_ranked.name: Schlittenbauer as the individual perpetrator
hypotheses_ranked.support: strongest documented motive/opportunity profile; file-internal contradictions (key, door) [2][6]
hypotheses_ranked.challenge: no linking evidence; police twice reviewed and did not charge; his odd remarks have documented innocent readings [2][6][7]
hypotheses_ranked.would_falsify: contemporary witness placing him elsewhere 31 Mar evening; DNA excluding him as Josef's father combined with closed maintenance dispute
hypotheses_ranked.uncertainty: speculative; preferred only within rank-1 family

hypotheses_ranked.name: Outsider robbery-violence (itinerants, ex-convicts, escaped Bärtl, Freikorps group, local thieves)
hypotheses_ranked.support: initial police line; missing paper money; stalking pattern (attic, tiles, snow traces); Weber's pre-crime robbery proposal [7]
hypotheses_ranked.challenge: coin left; coverings; multi-day animal care; Wiest's gain-exclusion; no loot ever traced (Kloiber 1926 lead died [7])
hypotheses_ranked.would_falsify: paper money accounted for in probate; traced loot item in outsider possession

hypotheses_ranked.name: Karl Gabriel returned
hypotheses_ranked.challenge: documented battlefield death [2]; key eyewitness story retracted as lie [2][6]
hypotheses_ranked.would_falsify: already substantially falsified for Gabriel personally

hypotheses_ranked.name: External serial-killer frameworks (e.g. 'Man from the Train')
hypotheses_ranked.support: none found in the file record

adversarial_self_audit: Covered bodies = known killer is a 2000-era behavioural inference, not a document; practical covering is equally plausible.
Robbery is not closed: paper money of unknown value vanished; hidden coin unfindable by a stranger fits the outcome.
The 'intimate knowledge' signal (attic straw bed, roof tiles) fits a long-hiding outsider at least as well as an insider.
'Lived with the corpses for three days' is literary amplification; intermittent presence or one later visit suffices for the observations.
Schlittenbauer's file is contaminated by mutual slander litigation with Sigl; companions' statements were partly reconstructed on request.
Multiple perpetrators explicitly remain open in the archival record [2].
The surviving record is copies of a partially burned, twice-reassembled file; absence of evidence may be loss of evidence.
The incest/paternity scandal may be a narrative magnet; an opportunistic outsider with untraceable paper money fits the physical evidence comparably well.
limitations: Original case file not examined; reliance on the 2026 archival exhibition catalog quoting it with page numbers.
Newspapers used via transcriptions, not digitized page images.
Leuschner (1978/1997/2007), Golla (2016), Edmaier (2007), Pötzl (1997) books not accessible online.
2007 student report not retrievable despite a stated public availability.
No DNA/exhumation project documentation found for 2023-2026.
